title: One loop, every kind
summary: Loop over PowerUsers and let each object answer for itself.

say.never: **Polymorphism** means "many shapes". An array of `Chargeable` can hold headphones, a phone and a tablet at once. When you call `getBatteryPercent()` on each one, each object runs *its own* version. Your loop never asks what kind it is.
say.bit: Call the promised method on each item; every object runs its own version.

say.never: `for (Chargeable thing : gadgets)` reads as "for each Chargeable *thing* in *gadgets*". It visits the items in order, with no index to count and no way to run off the end of the array.
say.bit: `for (Type item : array)` visits each item in order, no index needed.

say.never: It's tempting to write `if (thing instanceof Phone)`. Don't. Then every new kind of gadget means editing this loop. If you only call the promised methods, a brand-new class works the moment it says `implements`.
say.bit: No `instanceof` checks: only call the promised methods, so new classes just work.

marks.label: breaks when a new kind arrives

say.never: `totalAmps` keeps a running total and adds each user's `getAmps()`. `biggestUser` remembers the biggest so far, starting with the first one, and swaps only when it finds one that is strictly bigger, so a tie keeps the first. Check for an empty array before you look at `users[0]`.
say.bit: `totalAmps`: running total. `biggestUser`: remember the biggest so far; check for an empty array first.

say.never: Hold down **Ctrl** and tap **P**. A small search box pops up at the top. Type `PowerBudget`, then press **Enter**. It finds any file by its name, so you never have to dig through folders.
Your turn! Write `totalAmps`, then `biggestUser`. When they work, run `Main` and look at the robot's power budget.
